title: ONNX-EdgeIDS: A Lightweight Two-Stage Edge Serving Toolkit for Network Intrusion Detection
description:
ONNX-EdgeIDS is research software for deploying machine-learning network intrusion detection on resource-constrained edge devices. It provides Kafka and ZeroMQ replay for CICIDS2017-derived flow records, a first-stage anomaly gate that filters high-volume traffic, and a second-stage tree-ensemble classifier served by ONNX Runtime or by a dependency-minimal NumPy engine exported from the same ONNX graph, together with a release gate that checks the two runtimes agree before deployment.

This release hardens that gate. It builds its boundary probes from the ONNX graph itself rather than from the exported NumPy artifact, and before comparing any arithmetic it fails if the NumPy artifact differs from the graph (tree layout, thresholds, split modes, leaf weights, scaler and base values, equal once cast to float32) or does not declare float32 serving. The exporter and the NumPy engine now handle BRANCH_LEQ and BRANCH_LT splits as scikit-learn, LightGBM and XGBoost export them, one or two score columns, base values and the logistic or softmax transform; an optional set of exact-crossing probes straddles every split. On the shipped forest the gate's probes and results are unchanged (287,223 probes, 0 label disagreements). The research/ directory carries the experiment code and result files behind the accompanying papers.
